title: Dataset Versioning and Reproducibility: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Dataset Versioning and Reproducibility: Visual Guide

1. The Provenance Chain | six links from a deployed model back to immutable bytes, one of which is SQL text logged as provenance, plus the rollback pairing | every link must resolve to an immutable ID with a checksum, aliases must never rewrite history, and rolling back weights without feature versions recreates skew

2. Recipe Or Ingredients | the identical query replayed three months later against live tables and against a pinned snapshot, with four ordinary causes of drift | SQL text is a recipe rather than a captured ingredient set, and a long job reading a moving table produces internally inconsistent output that passes row-count checks

3. One Coherent Cut | three input tables publishing on different cycles, with a skew slider showing each task picking its own latest snapshot versus a release manifest | independently resolving latest per table mixes publication cycles into a dataset that was never simultaneously true, and pinning a snapshot is not point-in-time correctness

4. How Identical Is Identical | four levels of reproducibility from exact membership to bitwise identity, plus the four-level dataset diff | bitwise identity is often impossible because of floating-point reduction order and hardware math, so the level being claimed must be stated rather than assumed
